snapshot.note: used for the 2026-11-02 claims on Cercidiphyllum japonicum and Cornus nuttallii; the Acer palmatum claims stay on the 2026-10-26 snapshot (methods M6 — refresh is a decision for Kay)

data_notes: No date_planted field in the 2026-10-26 snapshot (earlier releases had one) — time_to_intended_size cannot be derived from this source until it returns.
height_m is a banded class, not a measurement: values cluster at 4.6 / 7.6 / 10.7 / 13.7 / 16.8 m (15 / 25 / 35 / 45 / 55 ft midpoints).
cultivar_name 'NONE' means not recorded, not the straight species.

methods.established_proxy: trees without a planting date: DBH >= 20 cm = 'established (DBH >= 20 cm, proxy)'; threshold written into each claim's value.threshold_dbh_cm and context; confidence 0.65, below the 0.75 of age cohorts for trees with date_planted; the two subsets are never combined (methods.md M2)
methods.cultivar_groups: cultivar label with n >= 50 gets its own claim group, context cultivar:'Name'; smaller labels stay in the species-level claims and are listed in their note; unlabelled trees are their own class cultivar:(unrecorded), never merged into a cultivar (methods.md M3)
methods.height_class: height_m is a banded class (15/25/35/45/55 ft midpoints); claims say 'height class' and set value.measure accordingly (methods.md M4)
methods.confidence: presence 0.95, counts 0.9, label frequencies 0.85, DBH 0.8, height class 0.75, age cohort 0.75, established proxy 0.65 (methods.md M1)

entities.name: Sun
entities.definition: Sites that receive six or more hours of direct sun in summer.

entities.name: Shade
entities.definition: Sites with little or no direct sun: filtered light under a canopy or deep shade on the north side of buildings and under dense trees.

entities.name: Part shade
entities.definition: Sites with roughly three to six hours of direct sun, or sun for only part of the day.

entities.name: Full sun
entities.definition: Six or more hours of direct sun in summer; no overhead canopy.

entities.name: Full sun only if soil kept moist
entities.definition: Takes full sun only where the soil does not dry out; in dry sun it scorches or stalls.

entities.name: Part sun/part shade
entities.definition: Three to six hours of direct sun, or dappled light for much of the day.

entities.name: Filtered shade
entities.definition: Light reaching the plant through a tree canopy or lattice all day; bright but never direct for long.

entities.name: Deep shade
entities.definition: Less than about two hours of direct sun; under dense canopy or on the north side of buildings.

entities.name: Sheltered
entities.definition: A position protected from strong or cold wind, for example near a wall or inside a planting.

entities.name: Acidic
entities.definition: Soil with pH below about 6.5, typical of coastal BC under conifers.

entities.name: Alkaline
entities.definition: Soil with pH above about 7.5, usually over limestone or where lime has been added.

entities.name: Bog
entities.definition: Permanently wet, peaty, acidic ground with standing water close to the surface.

entities.name: Humus rich
entities.definition: Dark soil high in decomposed organic matter; holds moisture and nutrients well.

entities.name: Rocky or gravelly or dry
entities.definition: Thin, stony or sandy ground that drains fast and holds little water or nutrient.

entities.name: Well-drained
entities.definition: Soil through which water passes freely, so roots are never left standing in water.

entities.name: dry
entities.definition: Little available soil moisture for long periods; relies on rain or drought tolerance.

entities.name: average
entities.definition: Ordinary garden moisture: rain plus occasional watering, neither dry nor wet for long.

entities.name: moist
entities.definition: Soil that stays damp but not waterlogged, such as a shaded bed or a slope base.

entities.name: wet
entities.definition: Soil often saturated: pond margins, ditches, poorly drained low ground.

entities.name: wide range
entities.definition: Tolerates anything from dry to wet once established.

entities.name: Dieback
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Dieback': Progressive death of shoots from the tips.

entities.name: Fungal leaf spot
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Fungal leaf spot': Spots on leaves caused by fungi.

entities.name: Galls
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Galls': Abnormal swellings caused by insects or mites.

entities.name: Leaf miner insect
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf miner insect': Larvae that tunnel inside leaves.

entities.name: Leaf scorch
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Leaf scorch': Browning of leaf edges from sun, wind or drought.

entities.name: Mealybugs
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Mealybugs': Woolly white sap-sucking insects.

entities.name: Mildew
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Mildew': Powdery or downy fungal coating on leaves.

entities.name: Mites
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Mites': Tiny sap-sucking arachnids causing stippled leaves.

entities.name: Mold
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Mold': Grey or sooty fungal growth on leaves or flowers.

entities.name: Nematodes
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Nematodes': Microscopic worms attacking roots.

entities.name: Root rot
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Root rot': Root decay from fungi in wet soil.

entities.name: Rust
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Rust': Orange fungal pustules on leaves.

entities.name: Scale insects
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Scale insects': Immobile sap-sucking insects under a waxy shell.

entities.name: Slugs or snails
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Slugs or snails': Molluscs that chew holes in leaves.

entities.name: Thrips
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Thrips': Tiny insects that rasp leaves and flowers.

entities.name: Virus
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Virus': Viral infection causing mottling or distortion.

entities.name: Whitefly
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Whitefly': Small white sap-sucking flies.

entities.name: Wilt
entities.definition: Pest or disease 'Wilt': Vascular disease causing drooping and death of branches.

entities.name: Plant Identity & Classification
entities.definition: What a plant is: its taxonomic identity (family, genus, species, cultivar) and its growth form.

entities.name: Plant Traits & Performance
entities.definition: What a plant needs, how it is built, how it behaves over time and what it does ecologically.

entities.name: Planting Design Knowledge
entities.definition: How plants are used in design: the vertical structure they build, the spaces they make, the way they are composed and the roles they play.

entities.name: Taxonomy
entities.definition: Botanical identity: family → genus → species → cultivar. Species are the plant records; cultivars are read from claims.

entities.name: Growth Form
entities.definition: The life form a plant is read as (tree, shrub, graminoid, herbaceous perennial, fern, vine) and the KPU plant type that records it.

entities.name: Environmental Conditions
entities.definition: The site conditions a plant needs or tolerates: light, soil, water, hardiness, wind; the habitat classes and BC biogeoclimatic zones it is recorded in.

entities.name: Morphology
entities.definition: How a plant is built: height, spread, form, habit, texture, colour.

entities.name: Temporal Performance
entities.definition: How a plant performs through time: growth rate, phenology (months), seasonality, leaf retention, photoperiod.

entities.name: Ecological Performance
entities.definition: Habitat and ecological value, origin and invasive status, resistance to stress, browsing, pests and disease, plus management and risk (maintenance, toxicity).

entities.name: Vertical Structure
entities.definition: The layers a planting is built from, top to bottom, and the height bands planting design works with.

entities.name: Space-making
entities.definition: How planting encloses and shapes outdoor space: screens, scrims, barriers and ceilings; degree, permeability and transparency of enclosure.

entities.name: Planting Composition
entities.definition: How individual plants are arranged into a planting: matrix, drift, group, scatter, layering.

entities.name: Landscape Use (KPU)
entities.definition: The documented use vocabulary: KPU's landscape-use facet as sources apply it to plants. The bridge from claims into the design concepts (maps_to, rule KG-R1); not a design theory in itself.

entities.name: Planting Roles
entities.definition: The job a plant does in a designed plant community: structural, seasonal theme, ground cover, filler, accent.

entities.name: Place
entities.definition: Where a claim holds or was observed: from the Vancouver scale outward.

entities.name: Time
entities.definition: When a claim holds: the plant's age at observation and the season or month of the record.

entities.name: Evidence & Sources
entities.definition: The claims, sources, conditions and verification status behind every link.

entities.name: Media
entities.definition: Images, GIS layers, planting plans and site observations that can be attached to a claim (`media[]`, schema 0.5.0).

entities.name: Family
entities.definition: The botanical family a plant belongs to, as recorded in its entity record.

entities.name: Genus
entities.definition: The genus, read from the scientific name.

entities.name: Growth form
entities.definition: Organising life-form classes read from the sources (M29), never inferred from 'Broadleaf evergreen'.

entities.name: Plant type (KPU)
entities.definition: KPU's plant-type facet, which mixes life form and leaf habit; kept as a trait.

entities.name: Light
entities.definition: Light the site offers, KPU's exposure facet with three groups (sun, part shade, shade).

entities.name: Soil
entities.definition: Soil types a plant takes, KPU's soil facet.

entities.name: Water
entities.definition: Water and drainage regime the plant needs.

entities.name: Hardiness (Canadian zones)
entities.definition: Canadian plant hardiness zones (KPU).

entities.name: Hardiness (USDA zones)
entities.definition: USDA hardiness zones as given by US sources.

entities.name: Hardiness (RHS ratings)
entities.definition: RHS hardiness ratings H1–H7.

entities.name: Wind exposure
entities.definition: Need for shelter from wind.

entities.name: Habitat class (E-Flora)
entities.definition: Habitat classes a plant is recorded in by E-Flora BC (normalised, M43); a shared class is an indirect connection, not a planting relation.

entities.name: BC biogeoclimatic zone
entities.definition: Biogeoclimatic zones (BEC) an E-Flora atlas page lists the plant in; CWH is Metro Vancouver's zone.

entities.name: Height
entities.definition: KPU mature-height classes; quantitative claims span the classes their range covers.

entities.name: Spread
entities.definition: KPU mature-spread classes.

entities.name: Form
entities.definition: Overall outline of the plant (KPU form facet).

entities.name: Habit
entities.definition: Branching and growth habit (KPU habit facet).

entities.name: Texture
entities.definition: Visual texture, fine to very coarse (KPU).

entities.name: Colour
entities.definition: Flower and foliage colours (KPU colour list).

entities.name: Growth rate
entities.definition: Slow, moderate or fast growth.

entities.name: Phenology (months)
entities.definition: Months of flowering or fruiting.

entities.name: Seasonality
entities.definition: Season of interest.

entities.name: Leaf retention
entities.definition: Whether leaves are held through winter.

entities.name: Seasonal interest
entities.definition: Seasonal interest features (fall colour, winter interest).

entities.name: Fruit
entities.definition: Fruit character (edible, showy).

entities.name: Photoperiod
entities.definition: Day-length response (survey c4; no source yet).

entities.name: Landscape use (KPU)
entities.definition: KPU landscape uses a source lists the plant for; the documented layer beneath the design concepts.

entities.name: Habitat & ecological value
entities.definition: Ecological values a plant offers: native, pollinator, bird food, cover, erosion control, habitat structure.

entities.name: Origin status
entities.definition: Native or non-native status for BC.

entities.name: Invasive status
entities.definition: Invasive-species listing status in BC.

entities.name: Stress tolerance
entities.definition: Abiotic stresses tolerated (drought, salt, wind, winter wet…).

entities.name: Browsing resistance
entities.definition: Resistance to deer and rabbit browsing.

entities.name: Pests & diseases
entities.definition: Pests and diseases, as susceptibility or as resistance.

entities.name: Maintenance
entities.definition: Maintenance level required.

entities.name: Toxicity
entities.definition: Toxicity to pets, humans or livestock.

entities.name: Plant age
entities.definition: Age bands of the plant at the time a value holds.

entities.name: Place
entities.definition: Geographic scale of the record.

entities.name: Vertical layers
entities.definition: The vertical layers of a planting: canopy, understorey, shrub layer, ground layer.

entities.name: Height bands
entities.definition: Robinson's five planting-height bands, from carpeting plants to trees.

entities.name: Spatial elements
entities.definition: Spatial elements planting can make: screen, scrim, barrier, ceiling.

entities.name: Composition patterns
entities.definition: Patterns for arranging plants: matrix, drift, group, scatter, layering.

entities.name: Planting roles
entities.definition: Roles in a designed plant community: structural, seasonal theme, ground cover, filler, accent.

entities.name: Cercidiphyllaceae
entities.definition: The plant family Cercidiphyllaceae, as recorded in the entity records of cercidiphyllum-japonicum.

entities.name: Cornaceae
entities.definition: The plant family Cornaceae, as recorded in the entity records of cornus-nuttallii, cornus-sericea.

entities.name: Dryopteridaceae
entities.definition: The plant family Dryopteridaceae, as recorded in the entity records of polystichum-munitum.

entities.name: Ericaceae
entities.definition: The plant family Ericaceae, as recorded in the entity records of arctostaphylos-uva-ursi, gaultheria-shallon, vaccinium-ovatum.

entities.name: Sapindaceae
entities.definition: The plant family Sapindaceae, as recorded in the entity records of acer-palmatum.

entities.name: Acer
entities.definition: The genus Acer, read from the scientific name; family Sapindaceae.

entities.name: Achillea
entities.definition: The genus Achillea, read from the scientific name; family Asteraceae.

entities.name: Arctostaphylos
entities.definition: The genus Arctostaphylos, read from the scientific name; family Ericaceae.

entities.name: Cercidiphyllum
entities.definition: The genus Cercidiphyllum, read from the scientific name; family Cercidiphyllaceae.

entities.name: Cornus
entities.definition: The genus Cornus, read from the scientific name; family Cornaceae.

entities.name: Gaillardia
entities.definition: The genus Gaillardia, read from the scientific name; family Asteraceae.

entities.name: Gaultheria
entities.definition: The genus Gaultheria, read from the scientific name; family Ericaceae.

entities.name: Polystichum
entities.definition: The genus Polystichum, read from the scientific name; family Dryopteridaceae.

entities.name: Vaccinium
entities.definition: The genus Vaccinium, read from the scientific name; family Ericaceae.

entities.name: Canopy
entities.definition: The uppermost layer: tree crowns that form the roof of a planting and shade everything beneath.

entities.name: Understory
entities.definition: Small trees and large shrubs that grow beneath the canopy and above the shrub layer (Robinson's low tree canopy / sub-canopy).

entities.name: Shrub layer
entities.definition: Woody plants branching from near the ground that fill the space between the ground layer and the trees.

entities.name: Ground layer
entities.definition: The lowest layer: herbaceous, carpeting and low woody plants that cover the soil.

entities.name: Ground-level planting (carpeting)
entities.definition: Carpeting plants at ground level. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

entities.name: Low planting (below knee)
entities.definition: Shrubs and herbaceous plants below knee height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

entities.name: Medium-height planting (knee to eye level)
entities.definition: Planting between knee and eye level: a physical barrier that still allows views over it. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

entities.name: Tall shrub planting (above eye level)
entities.definition: Planting above eye level: visual enclosure and screening. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

entities.name: Tree planting
entities.definition: Trees: canopy, ceiling and shade above head height. Bounds are approximate readings of the heading names (knee ≈ 0.5 m, eye ≈ 1.6 m) — to confirm against the chapter text.

entities.name: Screen
entities.definition: Planting that blocks a view: visual enclosure above eye level, opaque in the seasons it has to work.

entities.name: Scrim
entities.definition: A partly transparent screen: planting open enough to be seen through, which filters a view rather than blocking it. Term from the brief; not found under this name in Robinson, whose nearest heading is 'Permeability and Transparency of Enclosure' — to confirm.

entities.name: Barrier
entities.definition: Planting that stops movement: a dense, continuous physical enclosure, with or without a visual screen.

entities.name: Ceiling
entities.definition: Tree crowns forming an overhead plane that encloses a space from above.

entities.name: Matrix
entities.definition: A continuous ground-covering planting of one or a few species into which structural and seasonal plants are set.

entities.name: Drift
entities.definition: An elongated, irregular group of one species that flows through a planting.

entities.name: Grouping
entities.definition: Several plants of one kind set together as a block, group or mass.

entities.name: Scatter
entities.definition: Single plants distributed through a planting at random to give a natural feel.

entities.name: Layering
entities.definition: Combining plants of different heights so that canopy, understorey, shrub and ground layers occupy the same ground.

entities.name: Structural
entities.definition: Long-lived plants that give a planting its year-round framework.

entities.name: Seasonal theme
entities.definition: Plants that dominate the picture in one season and recede in others.

entities.name: Ground cover
entities.definition: Low plants that cover the soil between and beneath the others; the layer that carries most of the diversity and ecological function.

entities.name: Filler
entities.definition: Short-lived or fast plants that fill gaps while the framework establishes.

entities.name: Accent
entities.definition: A single plant placed for emphasis or focus: a specimen.

records.statement: Metro Vancouver's regional lawn watering restrictions apply every year from May 1 to October 15.

context.text: Metro Vancouver region (all member jurisdictions)

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

records.statement: Under Stage 1, residential lawns may be watered one day a week set by address parity (even: Saturday, odd: Sunday): automatic systems 5–7 am, manual watering 6–9 am.

context.text: Residential lawns, Metro Vancouver, May 1 – Oct 15

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

records.statement: Under Stage 1, trees, shrubs and flowers may be watered any day at any time by container, soaker hose, drip irrigation or a hose with a spring-loaded nozzle; sprinklers only 5–9 am.

context.text: Residential trees, shrubs and flower beds, Metro Vancouver, May 1 – Oct 15

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

records.statement: Watering a new lawn (or one treated for chafer beetle) outside the permitted times needs a municipal permit; the page gives no comparable rule for newly planted perennials or shrubs.

context.text: Metro Vancouver, during restrictions

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

records.statement: The restrictions do not cover rainwater, grey water, recycled water or other water from outside the GVWD/municipal supply.

context.text: Metro Vancouver

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

data.lead_time: at least one month before May 1

records.statement: Grass seed needs water for at least three weeks to establish, so Metro Vancouver advises overseeding at least a month before restrictions start on May 1.

context.text: Lawn seeding/overseeding, Metro Vancouver

sourceRefs.locator: verbatim quote kept in the local research copy (licence not cleared for publication)

records.statement: Metro Vancouver advises that an established lawn needs as little as about 2 cm of water a week (rain or watering).

context.text: Established lawns, Metro Vancouver; guidance, not a regulation
